suppression.implemented_by: a single function, cell(), in proof/build.py

published: sums only where the rule allows
postcode district (outcode) letters and digits with its public centroid
region, county, DNO / network region, public substation names

deterministic_techniques: the suppression rule is ONE function, cell() in proof/build.py; nothing else withholds
every withheld cell is counted and the counts are published here under suppression.tally
every data file carries its source, fetch time and sha256
all counts shown on the page are computed from the JSON at run time, never typed into HTML
URLs carry only permanent keys: ?district=<outcode>&sector=<SIC code>&lens=<name>
no randomness at all: proof/build.py and star.js import no random source
publication.json lists bytes and sha256 for every shipped file
proof/leak-check.py runs over every public file and its output is committed
proof/ci-checks.json states what the page must and must not contain, so CI can re-run it

links.why: the Quantum Twin Star and this star are built from the same estate grammar and palette and are read together.
this page uses the Star Generator's legend words, count sentence and colour vocabulary.
the Sun Star's supply-side figures can be read against the district demand counts published here.
the grid engine's relational map and these sector aggregates describe the same network from two directions.
every district centroid, region and county on this page comes from postcodes.io.

rules: no UK full postcode, except the published origin of the distance bands
no http outside globalgrid2050.com, ventusltd.github.io, postcodes.io, gov.uk, Companies House documentation and the local test server
no company name from the private source's name column anywhere in a public file
leak_check.note: run after every build; it exits non-zero on any hit, and its committed output carries the pass flag and the number of names tested

asserts: every lens tab at least 44 px high
the count sentence is present and built from the JSON
